analysis: What changed vs the 4 AM brief: the morning's two fresh prints both landed on the constructive side. Walmart beat and raised (adj. EPS $0.65 vs $0.64, revenue $188.8B vs $187.4B, FY guide lifted to $2.84-2.89) with U.S. comps accelerating to +2.9% — a consumer-spending read that runs against the week's hawkish-Fed gloom. Intel added a real company-specific catalyst: its first external 18A foundry customer plus an expanded Microsoft Azure deal, good for +4.4% premarket on a stock still ~60% below its 52-week high. Futures extended the 4 AM pop (Nasdaq-100 now +2.15%, S&P +1.25%) and the VIX compressed toward 22 from Wednesday's 24.56 close. The one crack in the tape is Apple, down ~2% premarket as iPhone 18 Pro demand worries resurfaced via a Jefferies note — but note the underlying order-cut report is the Oct 9 Nikkei story, unconfirmed by Apple, so treat the demand narrative as fragile rather than settled. Tesla's +1.7% on Musk's China-production pledge is a headline move, not a fundamental one. The Anthropic debut remains the day's center of gravity: the $26B private placement shows the AI supply chain buying its own customer's equity (Nvidia and Google $10B each), which is either partnership or circularity depending on your priors — the first trade will price that debate. Signal vs noise: Walmart's print, Intel's 18A customer, and the futures/VIX tape are signal; the size of the premarket pop and the ANT opening print are noise until the cash session confirms them.

community_signals.takeaway: The 922-comment Anthropic IPO thread remains the live debate, now reframed by the confirmed $83 price and the $26B supplier private placement: 'priced for perfection' skepticism at ~$1.5T vs AI-scarcity enthusiasm. It frames how the market may read ANT's first trade today.

headlines.headline: Walmart beat and raised before the open: fiscal Q3 adjusted EPS $0.65 vs $0.64 expected, revenue $188.8B (+5.2% YoY) vs $187.4B expected. U.S. comparable sales accelerated to +2.9% (from +2.6% in Q2), U.S. e-commerce +23%, and full-year guidance was raised to adjusted EPS $2.84-2.89 (from $2.80-2.87) and sales growth of 4.9-5.2%. Shares edged higher premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: A beat-and-raise from the biggest U.S. retailer is a direct consumer-spending read into the holidays — it leans against the week's cooling-demand narrative.

headlines.headline: Futures extend the rebound: at ~5:48 AM ET, Dow e-minis +0.67% (+335 pts), S&P 500 e-minis +1.25% (+92 pts), Nasdaq-100 e-minis +2.15% (+585.5 pts), with the VIX compressing to ~22.09 from Wednesday's 24.56 close. Prior session: S&P -0.23% for a fifth straight down day, Dow -1.11% for a third straight >1% drop, Nasdaq +0.42%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The snapback is strengthening into the open and volatility is coming off — breadth at 9:30 AM ET will show whether this is a durable turn or a premarket relief pop.

headlines.headline: Intel signed its first external customer for its 18A chipmaking process and expanded its Microsoft Azure collaboration, CEO Lip-Bu Tan said Wednesday evening at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin. Shares +4.4% premarket to ~$57.09 vs Wednesday's $54.67 close, after falling sharply since its Oct 29 earnings miss on the Q4 outlook.
headlines.why_it_matters: A first outside 18A customer is the milestone Intel's foundry turnaround has been waiting for — a company-specific catalyst on top of the broad chip rally.

headlines.headline: Apple down ~2% premarket as iPhone 18 Pro demand worries resurface: Jefferies flagged weaker demand and further component order cuts (10-15%) in a Monday note. The underlying order-cut report is Nikkei's Oct 9 story (October orders cut at least 15%), which Reuters said it could not verify and Apple has not commented on.
headlines.why_it_matters: Apple is the one Mag 7 name diverging from the rebound — single-source, unconfirmed by Apple, and the report is weeks old, so treat the demand narrative as fragile rather than settled.

headlines.headline: Tesla +1.7% premarket after Elon Musk said Tesla will continue increasing production in China, in a meeting with the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade, per Reuters citing Chinese state media. Musk is in China with the U.S. delegation for APEC week. Shanghai delivered 810,889 Model 3/Y through October, +21.4% YoY.
headlines.why_it_matters: A production-commitment headline out of China — single-source via state media — and a modest premarket lift; the Shanghai hub matters because it is Tesla's largest production base.

headlines.headline: Anthropic debut context: alongside the $81.3B public offering, a $26B private placement at the $83 IPO price was bought by seven suppliers — Google $10B, Nvidia $10B, AMD $2.5B, Broadcom $1B, Micron $1B, Microsoft $1B, TSMC $0.5B. Demand ran to nearly 7x the shares on offer, and 315M insider shares are eligible to sell from day one under a staggered lock-up.
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI supply chain is buying its biggest customer's equity — partnership to bulls, circularity to skeptics — and today's first trade prices that debate; day-one insider supply is a real overhang to watch.

headlines.headline: Nvidia +1.7% premarket, holding above $150 after closing Wednesday at $150.96 (-2.89%). The Q3 beat still stands — revenue $115.8B (+103% YoY) vs $109.1B expected, adjusted EPS $2.68 vs $2.48, Q4 guide $130B vs ~$125.1B — but the stock is ~36% below its Oct 6 high on the 71-72% Q4 margin guide, leadership questions, and Asia-sales uncertainty.
headlines.why_it_matters: The premarket bounce tests whether the post-earnings fade has bottomed — holding above $150 into the open matters more than the bounce itself.

headlines.headline: Gold stabilizing near $3,730 (+0.13%) after plunging 3.2% Wednesday to a 14-month low below $3,700, as the dollar index held near 19-month highs (~103.66-103.78) on the hawkish Fed minutes. The 10-year Treasury is ~5.08% (+1 bp) and the 2-year ~4.82%. December hike odds sit near 90% for 25bp.
headlines.why_it_matters: The metals flush and the strong dollar are the other side of the risk-on tape — if yields keep grinding toward 5.10% it caps how far the equity rebound can run.
